logp.method_description: The octanol/water partition coefficient, Po/w (or logPo/w), is a measure of the amphiphilicity of a material. It represents the relative solubilities of a given material in oil and water. The octanol/water partition coefficient Po/w of IrC1 was measured on an HY-4 oscillator according to a classical method. Equal amounts of n–octanol and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) were thoroughly mixed in the oscillator for 24 h. The mixture was then left to separate for a further 24 h so as to yield water and octanol phases, each saturated with the other. Complexes were carefully dissolved in PBS (concentration denoted as Co) and PBS saturated with octanol to form a 20 μM solution, respectively. The latter was then mixed with an equal amount of octanol (saturated with water) and shaken again as described above. After separation, the final Ir concentration of the complex in water was denoted as Cw. Both Co and Cw were measured by ICP–AES, and the partition coefficient (Po/w) for the complex was calculated according to the equation: Po/w = (Co–Cw)/Cw.
